answers.ask: What does matching the theme actually mean - running to the right section, wearing the right outfit, or collecting the right items?
answers.answer: Matching the theme means running to the section that matches the current theme.

answers.ask: What kinds of themes are the sections - biomes, colours, holidays, something else?
answers.answer: Make the sections different biomes, like forest, desert, snow, and beach.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D game map divided into distinct biome sections for running between: a forest, desert, snowy area, and beach, each visually separated and arranged as accessible zones around a shared central area.
agent_notes: A called theme with a correct section to run to is a round-based answer minigame, so Party & Casual, and the Quiz preset is what it builds even though the prompt never says quiz: a floor split into evenly identifiable answer sections plus a gathering space. The author confirmed the sections are forest, desert, snow and beach, which is dressing on tile-grid rather than a biome world — four themed floor sections in one arena, not four maps, so I kept space-bounded and stayed on P0 instead of reaching for world-biomes and its P4. I added trigger-scoring, which the preset lacks, because the whole mechanic needs each section to register who is standing in it. Deciding without a user: nothing named a lobby or separate staged round, so this is one continuous bounded space that players run around inside, and the run ends when the correct section is occupied rather than at a finish line.
